newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares down, further downside expected.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares down, further downside expected.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.21 percent on Thursday and traders said prices could slide further before the end of the year, ahead of a new tax on profits on securities which comes into effect next year.
The tax, which already applies to companies, is to be extended to individuals from January 1 1997.
The 10-share SBI index fell 2.53 points to 1,182.0.
"Turnovers and prices will probably go down by the end of the year," one trader said.
Turnover rose to 154.5 million tolars from 124.9 million tolars. Overall 11 shares fell, four rose, two remained unchanged and eight were untraded.
Drug maker Lek "A" issue was the most actively traded, falling 0.40 percent to 19,940 tolars on volume of 4,527 shares.
Lek dominated trading since September when it listed its "A" issue attracting foreign buyers to the bourse.
Traders said pharmaceutical companies and food producers will remain most attractive for foreign investors also in the next year.
Brokerage Dadas was the leading decliner, falling 14.37 percent to 8,520 tolars on volume of 71 shares.
Brokerage Nika was the biggest gainer, firming 3.48 percent to 4,128 tolars on volume of 3,185 shares.
